S.title: Weigh the Trade-offs - Community Builders of Pecan Grove
intro: The hearing is over. Before the Town Council decides, it weighs four paths.
Every path has good parts and hard parts. Help the town see them all.
There's no wrong path. Points come from weighing well.

S.tipWeigh: Next time, weigh all four paths before you choose.
S.tipGood: Next time, read the good parts slowly. Who would be glad?

S.real: Choose something your family is deciding, like a weekend plan. Name one good part and one hard part of each choice.
S.askQ: When you make a big choice, how do you weigh the good parts and the hard parts?
S.guText: There are four paths: build as planned, build with changes, don't build here, or wait for more information. Each has gains and costs, and each can earn full points. The score rewards exploring every path and naming who gains and who finds it hard. It never rewards the path chosen.

bank.b0005: Night nurse at the clinic on Main Street
bank.b0006: Farms next door; his well is close by
bank.b0007: Builds things; fishes in the creek with her kids
bank.b0008: Keeps the town's stories; her grandson needs work
bank.b0009: Runs the bakery on Main Street; pays town taxes
bank.b0010: Student who loves tech; has a little sister
bank.b0012: Then less well and river water is used.
bank.b0013: A wide strip of trees and land near homes
bank.b0014: Trees and distance soften light and sound.
bank.b0017: A plan for where workers will live
bank.b0018: So rents in town don't jump.
bank.b0019: A shorter tax break and a savings fund for the school
bank.b0020: The school still gets steady money.
bank.b0021: Set a clear date to decide
bank.b0022: Everyone knows when the answer comes.
bank.b0023: Money saved now to take it down if it closes
bank.b0024: No empty building is left behind.
bank.b0025: A truck route away from Main Street and the school
bank.b0026: Shoppers and school buses keep moving.
bank.b0027: An electrician class at the school
bank.b0028: Young people can train for good jobs nearby.
bank.b0029: Suggest an old factory lot instead of the farm
bank.b0030: New business could still come to town.
bank.b0031: The company pays for the studies

bank.b0033: Lots of building jobs start right away.

bank.b0036: A fast internet line could reach the clinic.

bank.b0038: Bright lights and a low hum near homes at night.

bank.b0040: Rents could go up while crews are in town.
bank.b0041: Building jobs, with a promise to hire people from here.
bank.b0042: A wide strip of trees between the building and the farm next door.
bank.b0043: The school gets a class to train electricians.
bank.b0044: Lights point down, so nights stay dark.
bank.b0045: The changes cost money, so the company asks to pay less tax for a while.
bank.b0046: Agreeing on every change takes months, and the work waits.
bank.b0047: If it closes someday, the empty building could stay.
bank.b0048: Lots of trucks on Main Street while they build.
bank.b0049: The farm fields and the creek stay as they are.
bank.b0051: The big pecan trees and the old places stay.
bank.b0052: Main Street keeps its usual traffic.
bank.b0054: No new tax money for the school.
bank.b0055: Main Street doesn't get new lunch customers.
bank.b0056: Young people may still move away to find tech jobs.
bank.b0057: Time to test the wells and the creek first.
bank.b0058: Time to look for old graves before any digging.
bank.b0059: Time to plan with the fire station for the big batteries.
bank.b0060: Time to study where the trucks would drive.
bank.b0061: Families next to the farm wait months to know what's coming.
bank.b0062: Building jobs, if they come, start later.
bank.b0063: The company could choose another town.
bank.b0064: The town pays for the studies.
